title: Phillies trade for Derek Hill from White Sox as they weigh moves to boost outfield
content:
In a move to bolster their thinning outfield, the Phillies acquired veteran Derek Hill from the Chicago White Sox in a marginal trade for two prospects on Thursday. It could be one of a few transactions the Phillies make to squeeze something more out of a struggling unit.

Hill, according to team sources, is expected to play center field and right field against left-handed pitchers. Sources indicated the Phillies had been in talks with Chicago about Hill before Adolis García’s right shoulder injury, suffered on Wednesday against the Toronto Blue Jays, and it remains unclear how much time García will miss.

The Phillies are sending prospects Dylan Campbell and Jose Colmenares to the White Sox. In addition to Hill, the Phillies are receiving $250,000 in international bonus pool money, sources said. They designated righty Jackson Rutledge for assignment to clear a 40-man spot for Hill.

The trade was first reported by ESPN.

Phillies outfielders have hit .240/.292/.377 this season and have been worth 0.1 WAR, according to FanGraphs, which is tied for last in the major leagues. Brandon Marsh has enjoyed a breakout season that has catapulted him into everyday status. Justin Crawford has struggled as a rookie and lost playing time against lefties, while García has been one of the worst hitters in the sport. He, at least, had played a strong right field until he departed Wednesday’s game.

Hill, 30, is considered a plus runner and defender. He has hit .213/.284/.375 in 90 plate appearances this season. Most of his time has come against left-handers; he has a .789 OPS against them. For his career, Hill has a .780 OPS against lefties. He has been used as a platoon player for much of his seven-year, big-league career.

It would make sense, then, if Hill were to form part of a platoon — potentially with Phillies outfield prospect Gabriel Rincones Jr., who would play against right-handed pitchers. Rincones missed the first six weeks of the season with knee inflammation. Although the 25-year-old prospect is off to a slow start with Triple-A Lehigh Valley, he is on the 40-man roster and could fill an immediate need. He would, at the very least, be a different option for the outfield mix.

Rincones was not in Lehigh Valley’s lineup on Thursday night. The Phillies were off and play Friday against the Brewers in Milwaukee.

The Phillies could also turn to familiar options in Otto Kemp or Felix Reyes. They have Bryan De La Cruz, a veteran of more than 400 big-league games, also at Triple A.

If García does not miss an extended period, Hill could simply replace Steward Berroa, who has been on the roster for the past few weeks as a speed and defense option. The Phillies have been carrying three catchers for weeks; they could opt to use Garrett Stubbs’ roster spot for extra outfield depth.

Campbell, 23, is the headliner in the return for Chicago. He can play all three outfield spots and some infield. But he’s struggled at Double-A Reading this season. Campbell will be Rule 5 draft-eligible after the 2026 season.
